issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: The problem statement and the template's example usage show animals being constructed with a single String name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). The solution implementation adds an extra int age parameter to Animal and to concrete animal constructors (e.g., Animal(String name, int age), Seal(String name, int age)). This prevents students who follow the problem/template (single-argument constructors) from matching the solution signatures and will cause confusion about required constructor parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirements consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and template examples to require and show two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and document the age attribute, or (B) remove the age attribute from the solution and change all animal constructors to a single-parameter form (String name) so they match the UML/problem and the template Main usage.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch: The UML and problem description specify that Animal has a name attribute (name: String) only. The solution's Animal class introduces an additional 'age' attribute (private int age) that is not present in the UML/problem statement. This inconsistency changes the class state students must set and leads to differing constructor and accessor expectations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal attributes with the UML/problem statement. Either remove the 'age' attribute from the solution (and its getters/setters/constructor parameter) so Animal only has 'name', or update the problem statement and UML to include 'age' and document its purpose, ensuring templates and examples reflect the attribute.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch and implicit attribute divergence: The template's Main (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java lines 9-12) shows creating Seal, Pig, and Goat with a single String argument (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). The problem statement/UML describes Animal with only a name attribute and states that each class should have a constructor initializing all attributes. However, the solution classes (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java, Pig.java, Goat.java) define constructors requiring two parameters (String name, int age) and the Animal implementation introduces an extra 'age' attribute. This inconsistency between expected single-arg constructors in the template/problem and the two-arg constructors in the solution will confuse students, may cause compilation errors when following the template Main, and forces them to reconcile differing constructor requirements across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructor requirements across artifacts. Either (A) update the template Main and the problem statement/UML to show and require two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and document the new 'age' attribute, or (B) modify the solution classes to provide a single-argument constructor Seal(String name), Pig(String name), Goat(String name) (e.g., by overloading constructors and assigning a default age) so the template Main compiles as shown. Prefer adding overloaded single-arg constructors in the solution to preserve the template examples, or explicitly update the UML and template to require the age parameter to avoid ambiguity.
